turns.content: I've taken up watercolour painting. Total beginner. Most of what I make is terrible but I'm enjoying it.
Enjoying the process regardless of the output is the right relationship to have with a new creative skill. What are you painting?
Mostly landscapes. I live near the coast so there's a lot of material.
Watercolour and coastal light are a classic combination. Are you working from photos or en plein air?
Photos for now. I'd like to paint outside eventually but I'm not confident enough yet.
Working from photos is completely valid — it lets you control the variables while you're building technique.
I've been doing a small painting a day for the last two weeks. Quantity over quality as a learning strategy.
That's actually excellent advice — it mirrors how musicians practice scales. Volume builds intuition faster than perfectionism.
